english.notes:
(i) Section 53A of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 was inserted into that Act by section 14 of the Policing and Crime Act 2009.
(ii) This offence is directed at a "punter".
(iii) Section 53A(2) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 provides that the following points are irrelevant for the purposes of this offence-
(a) where in the world the sexual services are to be provided and whether those services are provided,
(b) whether A "the punter" is, or ought to be, aware that C "the pimp" has engaged in exploitative conduct.
(iv) Section 53A(3) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 provides that "exploitative conduct exists if-
(a) C, "the pimp" uses force, threats (whether or not relating to violence) or any other form of coercion, or
(b) C, "the pimp" practises any form of deception.
(v) It would appear therefore, from Notes (iii) and (iv) above, that the prosecution does not have the burden of proving where a sexual service was to be provided, or if in fact it was actually provided. In addition there appears to be no burden to prove that the defendant ever knew or ought to have known of any force, threat, coercion or deception to induce or encourage the prostitute.
(vi) Although non imprisonable this offence now deemed PNC recordable by Secretary of State as from 30/07/2012. S.I. 2012/1713 refers.
